##### Graphs

A [*network graph*](#def-graph) is a set of nodes together with a weight for each ordered pair of them.  Whereas structural equations describe causal structure *within* observational units, network graphs provide a language for describing causal structure *across* units.  A network graph represents units as *nodes* and possible pathways of influence between units as directed, weighted *edges*: $\psi(i,j) > 0$ means that $j$ may influence $i$, and $\psi(i,j)$ need not equal $\psi(j,i)$.  Network graphs help us represent who is *eligible* to affect whom. The units that may influence $i$ form its *neighborhood*, $\mathcal{N}_i$.
